nodes.title: Resizing Reference Images
widgets_values: Each enabled reference is VAE-encoded independently and contributes its own native reference-token grid. Token count grows with image area, not only image count: doubling both width and height is roughly four times as many spatial tokens for that reference. References do not need to match the output canvas. Resize and crop upstream to the smallest dimensions that preserve the identity, style, palette, or detail you need. This workflow drives all ten loaders from one shared maximum dimension for convenience; ten is capacity, not a recommended starting point. Begin with one to three references and add more deliberately. JLC Load & Resize Image is convenient but optional.

nodes.title: ControlNet Orchestrator Notes
widgets_values:
The JLC Orchestrator builds one to four flat, non-recursive branches. Each slot has its own control image, strength, and start/end range while all slots share one loaded 2602 side-model checkpoint. Slot 1 is required. Strength 0 is an exact runtime bypass, although a cache layout that still selects that image may prewarm it unnecessarily.

Build from sparse to dense: establish DWPose/OpenPose first, add one auxiliary at low strength, shorten dense controls to early sampling when practical, and compare at a fixed seed. Depth, luminance, color, tile, and dense edges can overpower prompt, references, or inpaint. The shown values are starting points, not universal presets.

This example preprocesses at 4096 and then reduces the maps; that setting is aggressive and lower resolutions may be sufficient.

Sampler width and height define the target canvas. Control hints are prepared to that geometry; the source image does not automatically redefine both dimensions. A cache hit removes repeated hint VAE preparation, not per-step side-model work.

nodes.title: Experimental In/Out-Paint Adapter
widgets_values:
EXPERIMENTAL

Requires an active JLC ControlNet path and sits after the Orchestrator; the switchboard AND gate prevents standalone use. White/1 regenerates and black/0 preserves; the mask is hard-thresholded at 0.5. Image, mask, Empty Flux2 Latent, and sampler canvas must match exactly.

The sampler still starts from the clean empty latent—this is not partial-denoise img2img. Inpaint context is attached only to the first active ControlNet; other branches remain full-frame. Use sparse DWPose/OpenPose as host, keep dense auxiliaries low, and expect possible seed-variable edge artifacts.

After changing source aspect ratio, verify both resized width and the user Height match.

nodes.title: Conditioning Cache Prep — Exact Wiring
widgets_values:
CACHE WIRING — DO NOT SUBSTITUTE THE LATENT

The Cache Prep node must receive the same Empty Flux2 Latent that feeds the sampler. Do not connect the sampled latent or the latent entering VAE Decode. The empty latent defines the exact target pixel/latent geometry used to cache ControlNet hints and inpaint context.

Keep the selected slot counts, visible sockets, physical wires, and hidden input-layout contract synchronized. After changing reference_count, control_count, or use_inpaint, press Apply Input Layout and verify every exposed socket is wired.

The Conditional Save is the lazy branch gate:
TRUE requests cache prep and does not save.
FALSE requests inference and saves.

cache_ready_image is only a proof/routing token emitted after every active selected entry is ready. It is not a generated result.

A switched-off but physically wired branch may be pruned at runtime and is intentionally skipped. A genuinely missing selected wire remains an error.

nodes.title: Reference Tokens, VRAM, and Coherence
widgets_values:
Reference cost continues after caching. A warm cache avoids repeated VAE encoding and model load/offload churn, but it does not remove reference tokens from denoising. Every active ControlNet branch processes the expanded target-plus-reference sequence, so ten large references combined with several controls can remain much slower even on a cache hit. Fewer references and smaller reference dimensions are the first scaling levers.

Reference images are applied before ControlNet in this workflow. That order preserves native reference metadata while the JLC ControlNet path supplies exact-zero control padding for the reference-token suffix. Keep the reference set internally coherent: unrelated identities, incompatible clothing, conflicting camera angles, or contradictory styles may dilute the intended influence or create blended artifacts.

The reference cache is bounded, process-local CPU memory. It survives repeated queues only while the same ComfyUI server process remains open. A changed image tensor, resize, VAE, or cache contract creates a different key. Use “clear before run” only when you intentionally want to discard prior entries; an ordinary cache miss is safe and the runtime can refill it.

nodes.title: Note: JLC Boolean Logic (Frontend)
widgets_values: This node is not a standalone node. It is a frontend-only node intended for use with the ComfyUI Switchboard family of nodes. It is used here to ensure that the Inpaint group is enabled when the ControlNet group is enabled.

nodes.title: Cache Setup — Low VRAM
widgets_values:
LOW-VRAM TWO-PASS START
1) Set TRUE and queue once to prewarm the selected reference, ControlNet-hint, and active inpaint caches.
2) Return to FALSE and queue the normal workflow.
3) Repeat setup after changing source images, masks, output geometry, or VAE, or after restarting ComfyUI.
Leave “Clear image cache before setup?” FALSE for ordinary warm reuse. These are bounded CPU caches and do not survive a server restart.

nodes.title: TRUE = SET UP CACHE; FALSE  = RUN WORKFLOW
JLC Flux2 ControlNet — Read Me First
widgets_values:
JLC FLUX2 CONTROLNET — FULL WORKFLOW SHOWCASE

This workflow brings the main JLC Flux2 ControlNet features together in one place so you can explore them, mix them, and see how the pieces fit into a complete ComfyUI pipeline.

It is intentionally a full-featured showcase rather than a minimal starter workflow. Along with the core Flux2 ControlNet nodes, it uses optional utilities from the sibling JLC ComfyUI Nodes package and several common node packs to demonstrate reference conditioning, flat multi-ControlNet composition, experimental in/out-painting, cache prewarming, switchboard control, image preparation, and stage-boundary VRAM cleanup.

COMPATIBILITY

This package is designed for ComfyUI’s native FLUX.2-dev model path together with a compatible compact FLUX.2-dev Fun ControlNet Union / 2602 checkpoint loaded through the JLC Flux2 ControlNet Loader.

It is not a FLUX.2 Klein ControlNet implementation. Quantization by itself is not the deciding factor: this example uses an FP8-mixed Flux2-dev base checkpoint, but another checkpoint may also work when it preserves the compatible Flux2-dev architecture and ComfyUI runtime contract.

Model weights and external image preprocessors are not included with the package.

HOW THE WORKFLOW IS ORGANIZED

The main conditioning path is:

Prompt → Reference Image Orchestrator → ControlNet Orchestrator → experimental In/Out-Paint Adapter → guider and sampler

Use the switchboard at the upper left to turn Reference Images, ControlNet, and Inpaint on or off. The workflow automatically selects the deepest valid active stage, falling back through:

Inpaint → ControlNet → Reference Images → prompt only

Inpaint is AND-gated with ControlNet because the Inpaint Adapter extends an existing JLC ControlNet path and cannot operate as a standalone inpainting node.

THREE COMPLEMENTARY INFLUENCE SYSTEMS

• Reference images add native FLUX.2 reference tokens for appearance, identity, palette, materials, and related visual guidance.

• ControlNet adds structural or image-derived guidance through one to four flat, non-recursive branches that share a single loaded side-model checkpoint.

• Inpaint adds the Union model’s hard-mask context to the first active ControlNet branch. It works directly through the masked ControlNet conditioning path; it is not ordinary img2img partial denoising of a source latent.

WORK WITH THE SIGNALS, NOT AGAINST THEM

Prompt, reference images, control maps, mask, source image, pose, framing, and intended appearance should tell a reasonably consistent story.

More conditioning is not automatically better. When several strong inputs disagree, the model has to negotiate between them, and the result may become distorted, muddy, overconstrained, or simply strange. Start with the main influence you care about, then add references and auxiliary ControlNets one at a time while testing with a fixed seed.

OPTIONAL WORKFLOW UTILITIES

This showcase also uses JLC Load & Resize Image, Resize Multiple Images, Dynamic Multi Set/Get, Boolean Logic, Dynamic Aux Preprocessor Wrapper, Conditional Save Image, and Stage Boundary VRAM Cleanup.

These nodes help keep a large workflow organized and convenient, but many of them can be replaced with standard ComfyUI nodes or preferred third-party equivalents. The core JLC Flux2 ControlNet system does not depend on this exact presentation layer.

SAMPLING NOTE

The example is configured with an optional Turbo LoRA and eight sampling steps. Without that LoRA, use the sampler, scheduler, guidance, and step count appropriate for your chosen Flux2-dev model rather than treating eight steps as a universal recommendation.

VRAM CLEANUP NOTE

The Stage Boundary VRAM Cleanup node runs after sampling and before VAE decoding. On memory-constrained systems, it can help make room for the decode stage by unloading the connected model and clearing allocator leftovers.

That cleanup may also increase reload time on the next generation. It is an advanced, best-effort utility rather than a guaranteed VRAM reset, so feel free to bypass or remove it when your system does not need it.

The smaller notes throughout the workflow explain each section in more detail. A good first experiment is to begin with prompt-only generation, then enable Reference Images, ControlNet, and finally Inpaint as you become familiar with how each layer influences the result.
